message.content: The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**, which orbits the young star HD 100546. It has a mass of roughly **17–18 Jupiter masses** (about 0.017–0.018 solar masses) and a radius of about **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter**. This makes it one of the most massive “planet‑like” objects ever found, though its mass sits right on the boundary between giant planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs. In practice, the distinction is somewhat arbitrary, and many astronomers treat objects above ~13 M_Jup as brown dwarfs rather than planets.
